title: Residency ledger maintains a `win` rolling-sum no read ever consumes — dual bookkeeping, one source of truth
evidence: record pass: `r.win[key] -= u64(r.ticks[slot])` ... `r.ticks[slot] += 1; r.win[key] += 1`; read (port_residency_ticks) recomputes from the slot ring and never reads win values: `sum: u64 = 0; base := int(key) * RESIDENCY_WINDOW_TICKS; for s in 0..<RESIDENCY_WINDOW_TICKS { if r.slot_tick[base + s] > lo && r.slot_tick[base + s] <= tick { sum += u64(r.ticks[base + s]) } } return sum`. Grep over core/app/harness (incl. tests): `win`'s values are only written, resized, cloned (app/render/spawn_fx.odin:227), and length-checked (`if int(key) >= len(r.win)`), never read.
detail: Maintained-never-read state: extra work per record tick, a second (stale-inclusive) sum that can never substitute for the staleness-filtered read, and a misleading comment in port_residency_ticks that reasons about `win`. Same debt class the review swarm removed (`bundle_class_queue`).
recommended_fix: Delete the `win` field, its layout zero pass, and the two maintenance lines in residency_record_tick; keep the slot ring as the single source (bundle_tx_window's shape).

title: Undirected helpers `newest_in_bundle_lane` and `bundle_lane_ready` lost their last callers in this diff but remain
evidence: Definitions remain: `newest_in_bundle_lane :: proc(state: ^Run_State, cat: ^Catalogs, bi: u32, lane: u8, exclude: []int = nil) -> int` (line 425) and `bundle_lane_ready :: proc(state: ^Run_State, cat: ^Catalogs, bi: u32) -> (ready: [LANE_COUNT]bool)` (line 439). Repo-wide grep for call sites returns none; their former consumers were re-keyed: `shed_idx = newest_in_port_lane(state, cat, b, dir, l, drops[:])` (flow.odin:1245) and `ready := port_lane_ready(state, cat, bi, dir)` (flow.odin:1333).
detail: Dead twins left behind by the S2/S4 re-key. Unlike `bundle_lane_count` (still the sanctioned legacy view for stats P-rows and the S1-invisibility pin), these two have zero readers in production or tests.
recommended_fix: Delete both procs (or keep only if the render-heist legacy-view contract names them); note the removal beside the swarm's existing dead-code disclosures.

title: Review worktree carries an un-restored PERKINS-MUTATION-S3 — tree diverges from reviewed sha 1e9c783
evidence: Working tree (mtime 22:03, after tests-core.json 22:02): `demand := i32(1) // PERKINS-MUTATION-S3: demand unwired (uniform 1x)`. Reviewed sha / diff-core.patch: `demand := i32(1)` followed by `if int(class) < len(cat.packet_types) && cat.packet_types[class].bandwidth_demand > 0 { demand = cat.packet_types[class].bandwidth_demand }`. `git diff` shows exactly this one hunk.
detail: A mutation-leg leftover (not a defect of the reviewed diff): any later lens running `odin test core` in this worktree sees the S3 RED (streaming-transit pin fails) and could file false suite-red findings against a green head.
recommended_fix: Restore `core/flow.odin` to HEAD blob 998560b (`git checkout -- core/flow.odin`) before dispatching the remaining lenses; no code change to the PR itself.
